findings.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/common/base/header.scss:14 — The entire `.title { float: left; }` rule (not just the float property) was deleted; `.title`'s visual position within the now-flex `.contents` depends solely on implicit DOM order (default flex `order: 0`) rather than any explicit rule, making its left-most placement fragile/implicit compared to the prior explicit float

goldens.comment: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.
-ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.
-webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/common/base/header.scss:14 — The entire `.title { float: left; }` rule (not just the float property) was deleted; `.title`'s visual position within the now-flex `.contents` depends solely on implicit DOM order (default flex `order: 0`) rather than any explicit rule, making its left-most placement fragile/implicit compared to the prior explicit float

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `.contents` is converted to a flex container via `@include flexbox()`/`@include align-items(center)` and the entire `.title { float: left; }` rule is removed with no replacement (e.g., no `order` or flex alignment for `.title`). That does mean `.title`’s placement is now determined by default flex item behavior/DOM order rather than an explicit positioning rule. Whether this is actually problematic can’t be verified from the diff alone (no markup shown), so it’s a specific but non-defect concern.
